title: Property-based testing, QuickCheck style
description: Property tests assert universal properties (e.g., reverse(reverse(x)) == x) over hundreds of random inputs instead of hand-picked examples. The harness generates random inputs from strategies, checks the property on each, and reports the first failure; properties capture intent better than examples. It finds edge cases humans never write. Use it for archive utilities with clear invariants.
demo:
import random
random.seed(2)
def prop_reverse_twice(xs): return list(reversed(list(reversed(xs)))) == xs
fails = 0
for _ in range(200):
    xs = [random.randint(0, 9) for _ in range(random.randint(0, 6))]
    if not prop_reverse_twice(xs): fails += 1
print("property held on 200 cases; failures:", fails)
assert fails == 0

title: Invariant checking during test runs
description: Invariant checks assert data-structure properties (sorted order, balance) after every operation in a test. The harness wraps operations and verifies invariants like 'list stays sorted' after each step; violations pinpoint the exact operation that broke the structure. It turns unit tests into continuous proof. Use it when testing archive index structures.

title: Input shrinking for minimal failures
description: Shrinking reduces a failing random input to the smallest case that still fails, producing a readable bug report. Starting from the failing input, the shrinker tries smaller variants (fewer elements, smaller values) keeping only those that still fail; the minimal case usually exposes the bug's essence. Debugging starts from clarity, not noise. Use it to turn property-test failures into minimal reproductions.
demo:
def fails(xs): return sum(xs) > 10
xs = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
while True:
    shrunk = False
    for i in range(len(xs)):
        cand = xs[:i] + xs[i+1:]
        if cand and fails(cand): xs, shrunk = cand, True; break
    if not shrunk: break
print("minimal failing input:", xs)
assert fails(xs) and not any(fails(xs[:i]+xs[i+1:]) for i in range(len(xs)))

title: Random input fuzzing
description: Fuzzing feeds random and malformed inputs to archive programs to uncover crashes and hangs. The harness mutates valid inputs (bit flips, truncations, splices) and runs the target with timeouts; crashes are saved with their inputs for triage. It finds robustness bugs no test suite covers. Use it on every archive parser and decoder.

title: Mutation fuzzing of seed corpora
description: Mutation fuzzing evolves a corpus of seed inputs by random mutation, keeping mutations that explore new code paths. Each round picks a seed, applies stacked mutations, and runs the target under coverage; inputs covering new branches join the corpus. The corpus compounds toward deep program states. Use it for sustained fuzzing campaigns on archive tools.

title: Crash triage and deduplication
description: Crash triage groups fuzzer-found crashes by root cause so one bug is one ticket, not a thousand. Crashes group by stack-trace hash (top frames normalized); each group keeps the smallest reproducer. Dedupe turns fuzzer firehoses into actionable bug lists. Use it to manage findings from archive fuzzing runs.
demo:
from collections import defaultdict
crashes = [("parse", 12), ("parse", 12), ("index", 7), ("parse", 12)]
groups = defaultdict(list)
for loc, line in crashes: groups[(loc, line)].append((loc, line))
print("unique crashes:", len(groups))
assert len(groups) == 2

t: Test fixtures with setup and teardown
title: Test fixtures with setup and teardown
description: Fixtures build the world a test needs and tear it down afterwards, keeping tests isolated and repeatable. Setup creates temp dirs, sample archives, and connections; teardown removes them even on failure (try/finally or context managers). Tests never pollute each other or the machine. Use it for every test touching the filesystem or network.
demo:
import tempfile, os, shutil
def fixture():
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); open(os.path.join(d, "a.txt"), "w").write("x")
    return d
d = fixture()
try:
    assert os.listdir(d) == ["a.txt"]
    print("fixture ready:", d)
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(d)
assert not os.path.exists(d)
print("teardown clean: OK")

t: Mock objects for isolated unit tests
title: Mock objects for isolated unit tests
description: Mocks stand in for slow or external dependencies so unit tests run fast and deterministically. A mock records calls and returns canned responses; assertions verify the unit called the dependency correctly without the real service. Tests run in milliseconds with no network. Use it to test archive logic without live services.
demo:
class MockStore:
    def __init__(s): s.calls = []
    def fetch(s, k): s.calls.append(k); return f"data-{k}"
store = MockStore()
def get_record(k): return store.fetch(k).upper()
assert get_record("a") == "DATA-A" and store.calls == ["a"]
print("mock verified calls:", store.calls)
provenance: public-harvest: established computer-science methods documented in standard literature and practice

title: Parameterized test cases
description: Parameterized tests run one test body over many input cases, multiplying coverage without multiplying code. Cases live in a table; the harness expands each row into a test with a descriptive name. Adding a case is one table row, not a new function. Use it for archive functions with many input shapes.
demo:
cases = [("a", 1), ("ab", 2), ("", 0), ("hello", 5)]
def strlen(s): return len(s)
failed = [c for c in cases if strlen(c[0]) != c[1]]
print("cases:", len(cases), "| failed:", len(failed))
assert not failed

title: Line coverage measurement
description: Coverage measurement records which lines of archive code tests actually execute, revealing untested logic. sys.settrace (or coverage.py) logs executed lines; the report shows covered vs missed lines per file. Teams gate merges on coverage thresholds for critical paths. Use it to find untested corners of archive tools.
demo:
import sys
hit = set()
def tracer(frame, event, arg):
    if event == "line": hit.add(frame.f_lineno)
    return tracer
def target(x):
    a = x + 1
    if a > 2: b = a * 2
    else: b = 0
    return b
sys.settrace(tracer); target(5); sys.settrace(None)
print("lines hit in target:", len(hit))
assert len(hit) >= 3

title: Branch coverage tally
description: Branch coverage tracks which decision outcomes tests exercise, catching untested else-branches. The tracer records (line, next-line) arcs; branches never taken are reported. It is stricter than line coverage and finds half-tested conditionals. Use it for critical archive logic like parsers and money paths.

title: Coverage gating in CI
description: Coverage gating fails builds whose tests cover too little, making coverage a requirement rather than a wish. CI computes the coverage ratio and compares against the gate (e.g., 80% on changed lines); below-gate builds fail with the uncovered lines listed. Coverage ratchets up instead of decaying. Use it to keep archive tool test suites honest.
demo:
covered, total, gate = 85, 100, 80
ratio = 100 * covered / total
print(f"coverage {ratio:.0f}% vs gate {gate}% ->", "PASS" if ratio >= gate else "FAIL")
assert ratio >= gate

title: Golden-file regression testing
description: Golden-file tests compare program output byte-for-byte against blessed snapshots, catching any behavioral drift. The harness runs the tool on fixed inputs and diffs output against the golden file; mismatches fail with a diff, and intentional changes re-bless the file deliberately. Silent regressions become loud. Use it for archive generators and formatters.
demo:
golden = "line1\nline2\n"
def produce(): return "line1\n" + "line2\n"
out = produce()
print("matches golden:", out == golden)
assert out == golden

title: Flaky test detection by rerun
description: Flaky detection reruns suspect tests many times to distinguish real failures from nondeterministic flakes. The harness runs each failing test N times in isolation; consistent failures are real bugs, intermittent ones are quarantined as flaky with their failure rate. Flaky tests stop blocking the pipeline. Use it to keep archive CI trustworthy.
demo:
import random
random.seed(1)
results = []
for _ in range(20):
    results.append("fail" if random.random() < 0.1 else "pass")
rate = results.count("fail")/len(results)
print("failure rate:", rate, "->", "FLAKY" if 0 < rate < 1 else "STABLE")
assert 0 < rate < 1

title: Parallel test execution
description: Parallel test execution shards the suite across workers, cutting CI time from minutes to seconds. Tests partition by file or by historical duration for balance; workers run shards concurrently and results merge. Proper isolation (no shared state) makes it safe. Use it when the archive's test suite outgrows patience.
demo:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import time
def test_case(n):
    time.sleep(0.02); return n * n
with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    results = list(ex.map(test_case, range(8)))
print("parallel results:", results)
assert results == [n*n for n in range(8)]
